newsitem.title: EGYPT: Popular milling shares dominate Cairo bourse.
newsitem.headline: Popular milling shares dominate Cairo bourse.

text.p: Popular milling shares continued to dominate trading on the Egyptian stock market on Thursday but their prices ended unchanged or slightly lower, brokers said.

The millers raised turnover to an average 19.20 million pounds ($5.65 million) but failed to dampen the Capital Market Authority's (CMA) overall index which rose 0.25 points, or 0.12 percent, to close at 234.20.
"Trading was a bit quiet today. Prices in some of the milling shares were down because there is a lot of supply but they are all very good shares," said broker Yasser Rashed of Triple A Securities.
Central and West Delta Flour Mills again dominated activity, trading in shares worth 2.87 million pounds but the stock ended the day unchanged at 53.50 pounds.
The state privatised about 55 percent of the company's 7.5 million shares in August at 40.00 pounds each.
Heavy demand for privatisation of Central and West Delta Flour Mills persuaded the government to sell off more than 40 percent of its stake in milling shares, which it regards as strategic.
Upper Egypt Flour Mills was a close second, dealing in shares worth 1.84 million pounds but slipped 1.25 pounds to finish at 46.75.
The government sold to the private sector at least 40 percent of the company's seven million shares in September at 40.00 pounds a share.
East Delta Flour Mills, which was recently privatised, ended unchanged but saw trade in shares worth more than 9,500 pounds.
The state sold off 60.75 percent of the mills, after the flotation was 30 times oversubscribed.
The CMA index for openly traded firms rose to 359.31 points from 358.72 on Wednesday while the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 162.79 from 162.68.
